experiment: phase 9, child 8 - does an account mapping transfer between organisations?
corpus_covers: sha256 over every committed fixture in accountant/ingest/fixtures/, name then bytes, in accountant.ingest.sources.ALL_SOURCES order
taxonomy_covers: sha256 over accountant/taxonomy/*.py, name then bytes, sorted by name
configuration_covers: sha256 over pyproject.toml then ci/gates.toml, path then bytes

environment.git_commit_is: the commit every measured module came from; this branch adds only tests/test_cross_organisation.py and two artifacts, and changes no module under accountant/
environment.network: none - every byte read came from a committed fixture; accountant/ingest/fetch.py was not called

why_five_seeds: two runs in one process share a hash seed, so they cannot catch set or dict iteration order leaking into the output. Five seeds including one chosen at random can.

not_measurable.number: N2, review time as a fraction of read-everything time
not_measurable.reason: N2 needs R (seconds to read one entry) and D (seconds to dismiss one flag). Both are self-timed inputs and nobody has supplied them. The harness refuses to invent a default, and so does this manifest.

not_measurable.number: N3, catch rate per injected error type
not_measurable.reason: nobody injected errors into a real government ledger, so there is no answer key. The harness reports FAIL on absent evidence rather than a vacuous PASS.

the Department for Business and Trade publishes the narration column and leaves every cell in it empty. 0 of 28 committed rows load, all 28 rejected for empty narration, so DBT cannot be either side of a pair.
no Indian transaction-level ledger data is published. This corpus tests the mechanism and the transfer question only.
